name: Naming
desc: Guides for naming things in computer science.

resources.name: Gift wrapping algorithm
resources.desc: An algorithm for constructing the smallest shape that wraps a collection of points.

resources.name: Backtracking
resources.desc: When you explore a search space and you reach a dead end, you follow your _tracks_ back to the last crossroad and try the other way.

resources.name: Brute force
resources.desc: Violence is actually almost always a solution, but not a very clever one.

resources.name: Greedy algorithm
resources.desc: An algorithm that finds a solution by always picking the currently best-looking option without thinking too much about past and future decisions.

resources.name: Hill climbing
resources.desc: Starting somewhere in the hilly "landscape" of solutions, you go in the direction of steepest ascent until reaching the top of a hill. You might miss higher hills, though.

resources.name: Israeli Queue
resources.desc: A type of priority queue and a reference to the infamously unorganized queues in Israel. Here items can _cut in line_ when they _already have waiting friends_.

resources.name: Sieve of Eratosthenes
resources.desc: An ancient algorithm for finding all prime numbers up to a given limit. Non-primes are methodically sifted out, like unwanted material filtered through a sieve.

resources.name: Simulated annealing
resources.desc: An optimization algorithm inspired by the metallurgical process of annealing, where slowly cooling a heated material allows it to settle into a low-energy, globally optimal state.

resources.name: Adapter
resources.desc: Allows classes with incompatible interfaces to work together by wrapping its own interface around that of an already existing class.

resources.name: Decorator
resources.desc: Adds new responsibilities to an object by wrapping it in a layer of additional behavior, just as you can decorate a room without changing its walls.

resources.name: Facade
resources.desc: Analogous to a facade in architecture, a facade is an object that serves as a front-facing interface masking more complex underlying structure.

resources.name: God object
resources.desc: An anti-pattern where a single object knows too much or does too much. Like a god, it is omniscient and omnipotent.

resources.name: Promise
resources.desc: A representation of a result that is available in the future, unless there are errors. Like in reality, promises are broken sometimes.

resources.name: Shotgun surgery
resources.desc: A programming antipattern where, in a single change, you wildly add code everywhere in your codebase.

resources.name: Spaghetti Code
resources.desc: A program with a tangled and hard-to-follow structure.

resources.name: munch
resources.desc: Parser function that greedily consumes an input stream until it's satisfied.

resources.name: trampoline
resources.desc: Continuously runs functions that themselves return functions. Like a child on a trampoline that _returns_ and bounces back up.

resources.name: zip
resources.desc: Merges two lists into one list of pairs like the interlocking teeth of a zipper.

resources.name: Canary
resources.desc: A secret value placed on the stack to detect buffer overflow attacks. If it has been altered, danger is near — just like a canary in a coal mine that warns miners of toxic gas.

resources.name: Computer virus
resources.desc: A computer program that self-replicates by _infecting_ other computer programs, similar to the behavior of biological viruses.

resources.name: Cyber hygiene
resources.desc: Steps and practices that users should take to maintain system health and improve online security.

resources.name: Phishing
resources.desc: Refers to the use of lures to "fish" for sensitive information.

resources.name: Phoning home
resources.desc: When a system (e.g. stolen computer) secretly reports back to a third party other than the current possessor. The name is a reference to the movie E.T.

resources.name: Spear phishing
resources.desc: A targeted, personal phishing attack to trick a specific individual or organization into believing that they are legitimate.

resources.name: Confusion matrix
resources.desc: A tabular summary of a classifier's "confusion", i.e., how often it thought to make correct predictions when it actually didn't.

resources.name: Decision boundary
resources.desc: A boundary dividing the space of possible data points. Here you decide, everything on this side is SPAM, everything on that side is not.

resources.name: Gradient descent
resources.desc: Minimizing a cost function by iteratively computing the gradient and moving in the direction of steepest descent.

resources.name: Training
resources.desc: The process of showing the machine a bunch of examples, until it learns what we want from it.

resources.name: Choreographic programming
resources.desc: A programming paradigm where programs are compositions of interactions among multiple concurrent participants.
resources.section: Programming Languages and Programming Language Theory

resources.name: Clojure
resources.desc: A functional language making extensive use of closures but with a j because it's running on the Java virtual machine.
resources.section: Programming Languages and Programming Language Theory

resources.name: C++
resources.desc: Although C was certainly a bad name, C++ was quite clever. The iconic increment operator ++ indicates that C++ is the successor.
resources.section: Programming Languages and Programming Language Theory

resources.name: Lazy evaluation
resources.desc: An evaluation strategy which suspends evaluation until it's absolutely necessary and then never does it again.
resources.section: Programming Languages and Programming Language Theory

resources.name: Syntactic sugar
resources.desc: Syntax that makes the language "sweeter" for human use. Usually a shorthand for common operations that can also be expressed in a more verbose form.
resources.section: Programming Languages and Programming Language Theory

resources.name: Busy Beaver
resources.desc: Turing machines that produce numbers so insanely large, no other algorithm can keep up with them.

resources.name: Clique problem
resources.desc: The problem of finding groups of mutual friends in a network of people with friendship relations. Or more generally, finding complete subgraphs.

resources.name: Game of Life
resources.desc: A game world that showcases how astonishing complexity can arise from very simple ingredients.

resources.name: Oracle
resources.desc: A black box that magically gives answers even to undecidable questions like the halting problem.

resources.name: Pumping lemma
resources.desc: The fact that in some formal languages any sufficiently long string can be _pumped_ with repetitions of its substring and the result stays in the same formal language.

resources.name: bubblewrap
resources.desc: Sandboxing tool forming a protective layer for your system.

resources.name: caffeinate
resources.desc: Terminal app to keep macOS from "sleeping".

resources.name: clooney
resources.desc: A JavaScript library implementing the actor model for concurrent computation. The term is a reference to George Clooney, who is also an actor.

resources.name: CockroachDB
resources.desc: Database application, that is marketed as being so fault-tolerant and resilient as a cockroach.

resources.name: corrosion
resources.desc: The process that turns metal into rust (literally), but also a tool that "turns" C++ into Rust.

resources.name: git bayesect
resources.desc: Like git bisect but can cope with flaky tests using Bayesian inference.

resources.name: go-brrr
resources.desc: Pure Go implementation of the _br_otli compression algorithm. Also a reference to the go brrr meme.

resources.name: horcrux
resources.desc: Splits a file into encrypted fragments that only together can be decrypted again. In the Harry Potter universe, Horcruxes are fragments of a person's soul. To kill the person, all fragments must be destroyed.

resources.name: Puppeteer
resources.desc: A browser automation library. If the browser is the puppet, this is the puppeteer.

resources.name: tldr
resources.desc: Simplified man pages with practical examples.

resources.name: Uglify
resources.desc: A JavaScript minifier. Removes everything that makes the code readable and pretty to make it smaller.

resources.name: uppy
resources.desc: A dog-themed uploader component. The name is a blend of _upload_ and _puppy_. It even comes with a crash recovery plugin called _Golden Retriever_.

resources.name: Webpack
resources.desc: A bundler for JavaScript and other _web_ assets with a short and descriptive name that also somewhat rhymes.

resources.name: yarn
resources.desc: Node.js dependency manager.

resources.name: Bento layout
resources.desc: A grid-based layout resembling the compartmentation of bento boxes.

resources.name: Carousel
resources.desc: A kind of animated slideshow looping back on itself.

resources.name: Desktop
resources.desc: The metaphorical top of the user's desk, upon which objects such as documents and folders of documents can be placed.

resources.name: Hamburger button
resources.desc: A button to toggle a menu. The associated icon resembles a hamburger.

resources.name: Optimistic UI
resources.desc: User interfaces that assume expensive operations will complete successfully, thereby improving the perceived performance.

resources.name: Scrolling
resources.desc: Screen content is often less like a book with discrete pages and more like a continuous roll of parchment, i.e., a scroll.

resources.name: Toast notification
resources.desc: A small message that briefly pops up at the edge of the screen and then disappears on its own, just like toast from a toaster.

resources.name: a11y, i18n, k8s, ...
resources.desc: Abbreviating long words by keeping the first and last letter and writing the number of omitted letters in between.

resources.name: ACID vs. BASE
resources.desc: Acronyms describing competing database ideologies (aka. SQL vs. NoSQL). Note that acid and base are also opposites in chemistry.

resources.name: Bottleneck
resources.desc: A central part of a network/application that significantly limits throughput/performance and should ideally be eliminated.

resources.name: camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case
resources.desc: Different case styles where the name illustrates its appearance.

resources.name: Code golf
resources.desc: Writing a program in as few characters as possible. Just like how Golf players try to win in the fewest club strokes.

resources.name: Cookie licking
resources.desc: E.g., claiming a GitHub issue, then not working on it.

resources.name: Firmware
resources.desc: The _ware_ between _software_ and _hardware_.

resources.name: Floating point number
resources.desc: This representation can encode numbers at very different magnitudes with a limited amount of digits by letting the radix point _float_ instead of being fixed in place.

resources.name: Framework
resources.desc: In software architecture (like in actual architecture), frameworks provide a basic structure to build upon, guiding and constraining further development.

resources.name: Glue Code
resources.desc: Jenga and LEGO bricks don't share the same interface, but you can always glue them together.

resources.name: Great Firewall of China
resources.desc: Chinas controversial internet censorship system and a reference to the Great Wall of China.

resources.name: Heisenbug
resources.desc: A bug that seems to disappear or change when one tries to study it. It's a pun on Werner Heisenberg, who discovered that the act of observing quantum systems inevitably alters their state.

resources.name: Hydra
resources.desc: A bug that, when an attempt to fix it is made, introduces multiple new bugs. It's a bug that cannot be fixed.

resources.name: Technical debt
resources.desc: The implied future cost of shortcuts taken today, which accumulates like financial debt and must eventually be paid back — often with interest.

resources.name: Time travel debugging
resources.desc: Stepping back in time through source code to understand execution and sometimes even to change history.

resources.name: Tree shaking
resources.desc: Shake the dependency tree until all the dead parts are falling off and you end up with a nice lean tree.

resources.name: Unfair enumeration
resources.desc: A program that outputs all even numbers and then all odd numbers generates an unfair enumeration of the natural numbers because some numbers are never reached.

resources.name: Yoda condition
resources.desc: When you write if ("red" === color) { instead of if (color === "red") { because it reads as, “if red equals the color”, similar to the way the Star Wars character Yoda speaks.
